---
applyTo: '.github/workflows/*.yml'
---

# Workflow Notes for AI Agents

## .github/workflows/

- `CI.yml` covers the same ground as local `make check` (which runs `make tidy`, the pre-commit hooks, and tests), but fans it out across four parallel jobs: `secrets` (trufflehog, then `nox -s secrets` on the staged change), `precommit` (`nox -s precommit`), `analysis` (`nox -s analysis`, which runs the `ty`, `basedpyright` and `pylint` hooks) and `pytest` (`nox -s test`). The analysis hooks are the slowest in the config, so they have their own job rather than lengthening `precommit`. CI runs `.github/scripts/ci-ruff-args.sh` before the pre-commit session to give ruff stricter arguments and GitHub-formatted output, while local `make check` uses the arguments in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
- **`run-ci` (`Run CI (3.13)`) is the context `main` requires, through the ruleset `main-protect`, and its name is load-bearing.** Renaming the job leaves a required context that never reports, which blocks every pull request, and renaming it to something not required silently un-gates the branch. Check `gh api repos/michen00/pr-checks/rulesets` before touching it. The job set can otherwise grow freely behind it; `tests/test_ci_jobs.py` fails if a job is left out of its `needs`.
- `bot-automerge.yml` approves each Dependabot pull request as github-actions[bot] and arms auto-merge on it once every commit on it is GitHub-signed, every commit other than a merge is Dependabot's own, every merge is a clean merge of two parents or authored by a repository admin, every commit a push by anyone but Dependabot or an admin added (beyond the default branch's own) is a clean merge of two parents, Dependabot reports an update type, and a ruleset on the base branch requires `Run CI (3.13)`. A rewrite pushed by anyone else holds the pull request. It runs only on `opened` and `synchronize`, the events that bring commits: a label change or a reopen carries no pusher, so a run on one would vouch for a head the pusher rule held on its push. Removing `do not auto-merge` or reopening therefore re-arms nothing; `@dependabot rebase` does, through a checked push. Majors are included. The check reads the head commit once and holds if the head moves while it runs; the approval names that commit through the reviews API, and arming uses `--match-head-commit`, so neither acts on a later push. A last step, on `always()`, turns off auto-merge that an earlier run armed whenever a run does not trust the head (including a run that failed first) or finds CI no longer required; a hold on the update type alone leaves it, since a person may have armed it. To recompute merges, the job checks out the default branch and fetches the pull request's commits as objects only, so nothing from the pull request runs. The approval is never the App's: where the base branch requires approval of the most recent push, an approval counts only from an identity other than the last pusher, and a catch-up merge would push as the App. It arms as the App when `vars.APP_CLIENT_ID` and `secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY` are set, so the merge's push to `main` starts workflows; a Dependabot-triggered run reads only the Dependabot secret store, so the key must be in both stores. Its steps receive the App's key, so its actions are pinned to commits, which Dependabot moves. The `do not auto-merge` label withholds arming, and `bot-automerge-disarm.yml` turns auto-merge off on any pull request that receives it. `tests/test_workflows.py` pins the CI gate, the approval identity and commit, the author check, both merge paths, the pusher rule, the head check, the fail-closed disarm and the disarm trigger, and holds both workflows to checking out nothing from the pull request, since they are the only `pull_request` workflows with a write scope.
- **No hook may pass by scanning nothing.** gitleaks reads only staged changes, so under `pre-commit run --all-files` on a clean checkout it scans nothing and passes. The `precommit` job skips it, and the `secrets` job resets the checkout softly to the comparison base (the pull request's base, or the commit before a push), so the whole change is staged, then runs `nox -s secrets`, which fails when nothing is staged rather than passing. `tests/test_ci_jobs.py` checks that the job stages before it scans. A dispatched run has no base, so only trufflehog scans it.
- ty, basedpyright and pylint run in the `analysis` job, through their pre-commit hooks at the default stage, and the `precommit` job skips them with `SKIP`. That `SKIP` names the hook ids in `noxfile.py`'s `_ANALYSIS_HOOKS` and `_SECRET_HOOKS`, and `tests/test_ci_jobs.py` fails if they part. The ty hook syncs `uv.lock`, with every dependency group, into the project environment and checks against it; ty's version comes from the hook's `rev`, not from `uv.lock`. basedpyright and pylint run as local hooks through `uv run --locked --all-groups`, so their versions come from `uv.lock`, and `pyrightconfig.json` and `.pylintrc` enable only the checks ruff and ty do not make.
- **Coverage report.** CI's `pytest` job writes a coverage JSON, diffs the branch against its comparison base, renders `coverage/report.md` with `scripts/coverage_diff_report.py` (how many of the changed lines a test ran, else the repository totals), and uploads it as the `coverage-report` artifact. No workflow posts it as a comment yet. Nothing fails on a coverage number.
- Cache resets rely on a new `.github/workflows/.cache-buster` (see `make bust-ci-cache`, which writes the time and a random UUID, so no two busts match). That file is folded into every cache key, so a new one invalidates them all, and `tests/test_workflow_caches.py` fails if a cache leaves it out. The pre-commit caches lead with the buster, then the hook config: a changed config restores the newest entry under the same buster through `restore-keys`, so only the hooks whose rev moved are built again, and `pre-commit gc` drops what the config no longer uses before the entry is saved. Each job keeps its own uv cache entry (`cache-suffix: ${{ github.job }}`), because the jobs install different dependency groups and an existing key is never saved again. Each job installs only the `ci` dependency group (nox and pre-commit) for itself; the `test` session installs its own group.
- Hook version bumps are Dependabot's job via the `pre-commit` ecosystem in `.github/dependabot.yml`.
- **Every `uses:` must be pinned to a full commit SHA with its exact release in a trailing comment** (`actions/checkout@<40 hex> # v7.0.1`), the form Dependabot's `github-actions` ecosystem moves together, and every `actions/checkout` must set `persist-credentials: false`. `tests/test_workflow_pins.py` enforces both. The one exception is a `docker://` image, which must name an exact version: Dependabot's `github-actions` parser skips `docker://` references, and its `docker` ecosystem reads Dockerfiles and Kubernetes manifests, so no form of the reference would be updated automatically.
- `lint-github-actions.yml` is `workflow_dispatch`-only: actionlint is already enforced on every pull request into `main` and every push to `main` by its pinned pre-commit hook, which CI runs. Keep the workflow's pinned image tag in step with the hook's `rev`, by hand.
- **Documentation Consistency:** Keep guidance documents (`AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.github/instructions/CI.instructions.md`, `.specify/memory/constitution.md`, and `README.md`) consistent with workflow behavior, and change them in the same commit as the workflow.
